newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Iran minister invites UAE leader to Islamic summit.
newsitem.headline: Iran minister invites UAE leader to Islamic summit.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Wednesday invited United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan to an Islamic summit meeting in Tehran, the official news agency WAM said.
Velayati also discussed bilateral issues and Middle East and other regional developments during a meeting with UAE Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Sultan bin Zaid al-Nahayan, it said.
He arrived in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, the last leg of a six-nation Gulf tour that took him to Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Oman to deliver summit invitations.

"During their meeting, his highness received a verbal invitation from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani to Sheikh Zaid to attend the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) summit in Tehran in December," WAM said.

Sheikh Sultan reiterated the UAE's support for the OIC, the Moslem world's biggest body, and "its participation in all meetings and activities to serve the causes of the Islamic Umma (nation)", it added.
He also expressed hope that the next summit will succeed to help boost joint Islamic work.

Iran and the UAE have been at loggerheads since 1992 due to a territorial dispute over the islands of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs that are close to key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.
Iran's relations with its Gulf Arab neighbours are often tense. Gulf Arab states have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge which Iran denies.
Velayati arrived from Manama, where he asked Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa to come to the summit.

Bahrain last year accused Shi'ite Moslem Iran of backing an attempt to topple its government by force. Iran denied the charge. The trial of 81 people accused of involvement in the alleged plot began earlier this month.
